Class Camera

java.lang.Object
renderer.Camera
All Implemented Interfaces:
Cloneable
public class Camera extends Object implements Cloneable
Represents a camera in 3D space.

The camera is responsible for generating rays through a pixel grid that represents the view plane. It uses the Builder pattern for construction and supports configuring the view plane, resolution, ray tracer, multi-threading, anti-aliasing, and depth-of-field.

Super-sampling dispatch priority inside castRay(int, int):

  1. Depth-of-field beam (when apertureSize > 0)
  2. Anti-aliasing beam (when antiAliasingNumSamples > 1)
  3. Single central ray (default — original behavior)

    • _threadsCount

      private int _threadsCount
      Thread count for parallel rendering.
      • 0 – single-threaded (default)
      • -1 – Java parallel stream (JVM auto-detects core count)
      • -2 – raw threads, count = logical cores − SPARE_THREADS
      • ≥1 – raw threads, explicit count

    • SPARE_THREADS

    • _printInterval

      private double _printInterval
      Progress-print interval expressed as a percentage of total pixels rendered. 0 suppresses all progress output.

    • _pixelManager

      private PixelManager _pixelManager
      Shared pixel manager that distributes pixels across threads and tracks rendering progress. Initialized at the start of renderImage().

    • _antiAliasingNumSamples

      private int _antiAliasingNumSamples
      Number of sample rays cast through random / grid positions inside each pixel for anti-aliasing. 1 = disabled (a single central ray is used, identical to the original single-ray behavior).

    • _apertureSize

      private double _apertureSize
      Radius of the simulated aperture window. 0 = disabled (pinhole camera — no depth-of-field blur). Larger values produce stronger out-of-focus blur.

    • _focalDistance

      private double _focalDistance
      Distance from the camera along _vTo to the focal plane. Objects located exactly on this plane appear sharp; objects at other distances are blurred proportionally to their offset from the plane. Default: 100 world units.

    • _dofNumSamples

      private int _dofNumSamples
      Number of aperture sample points used per pixel during depth-of-field rendering. More samples → smoother blur, longer render time. Default: 81 (equivalent to a 9 × 9 grid).

    • _samplingPattern

      private Blackboard.SamplingPattern _samplingPattern
      Point distribution pattern used when building a Blackboard for any camera-level super-sampling feature (anti-aliasing or depth of field). Default: Blackboard.SamplingPattern.GRID.

    • _targetShape

      private Blackboard.TargetShape _targetShape
      Target area shape used when building a Blackboard for any camera-level super-sampling feature. Default: Blackboard.TargetShape.SQUARE.

      private Point getPixelCenter(int xIndex, int yIndex)
      Computes and returns the world-space center point of the pixel at column xIndex, row yIndex.

      Extracted from constructRay(int, int) so that both single-ray rendering and all super-sampling beam generators can reuse the same pixel-center formula without duplicating code.

      Parameters:
      xIndex - pixel column index (0-based, left to right)
      yIndex - pixel row index (0-based, top to bottom)
      Returns:
      the 3D center of the specified pixel on the view plane

    • castRay

      private void castRay(int xIndex, int yIndex)
      Computes and writes the color for a single pixel, then signals the PixelManager that the pixel is complete (for progress tracking).

      Super-sampling dispatch priority:

      1. Depth-of-field beam – activated when _apertureSize > 0.
      2. Anti-aliasing beam – activated when _antiAliasingNumSamples > 1.
      3. Single central ray – the original single-ray behavior (default).
      Parameters:
      xIndex - pixel column index
      yIndex - pixel row index

    • computeColorAntiAliasing

      private Color computeColorAntiAliasing(int xIndex, int yIndex)
      Computes the anti-aliased color for a pixel by tracing multiple rays through sample points distributed across the pixel area and averaging the results.

      The sampling region is centered at the pixel center on the view plane. Its half-extent is min(rx, ry) / 2 so that all sample points remain within the pixel boundary regardless of the pixel aspect ratio. The region's orientation uses the camera's own right/up vectors as basis.

      Parameters:
      xIndex - pixel column index
      yIndex - pixel row index
      Returns:
      the averaged color for this pixel

    • computeColorDoF

      private Color computeColorDoF(int xIndex, int yIndex)
      Computes the depth-of-field color for a pixel by tracing rays from multiple sample points on the aperture window, all converging toward the same focal point, and averaging the results.

      Focal point computation: the central pixel ray is intersected with the focal plane — a plane perpendicular to _vTo at distance _focalDistance from the camera. This guarantees all focal points lie on a true flat plane and not on a curved surface (which would distort the image).

      Aperture sampling: a Blackboard centered at the camera origin (_p0), with radius _apertureSize, generates the aperture sample points. The aperture lies in the same plane as the camera (spanned by _vRight and _vUp).

      Parameters:
      xIndex - pixel column index
      yIndex - pixel row index
      Returns:
      the averaged depth-of-field color for this pixel
